rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion approach (the core hypothesis of this study) can outperform single-modality baselines, and which component choices yield a strong starting point. config_001 tests a well-motivated multimodal configuration: scvi_n200 (a well-established deep generative encoder for scRNA-seq), imagenet_vit_l (the stronger image encoder), avgpool (robust, low-variance aggregation), and weighted fusion (principled modality balancing). This establishes a strong baseline in the multimodal space. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual choices (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion type) or compare against rna_only/image_only baselines. If it underperforms, we learn that multimodal fusion may not be the right direction and can pivot. As experiment 1 of 10, this maximizes information gain about the most fundamental design axis (modality combination) while using components most likely to perform well, avoiding a wasted experiment on a weak configuration.

With only one data point (config_001: multimodal, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted → 0.706 acc), the largest uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion actually adds value over a single modality. Config_008 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) uses the identical image encoder and aggregation as config_001, so any accuracy difference isolates the contribution of the RNA modality. If image-only is near 0.706, the RNA signal is marginal and I should pivot to optimizing the image pipeline; if it is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed as the right direction and I can exploit the remaining 7 experiments on RNA encoder, fusion strategy, and aggregation choices within the multimodal space. This single experiment resolves the most consequential architectural question before committing budget to fine-grained hyperparameter search.

Evidence: config_001 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieved 0.706 accuracy, dramatically outperforming image-only config_008 (0.332), confirming multimodal fusion with these encoders is the right direction. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the avgpool aggregation is optimal or whether a transformer-based aggregation could better capture cross-modal interactions between the RNA and image features. This experiment (config_012) makes a single-variable change—swapping avgpool for transformer aggregation—while holding all other components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion, multiprofile) identical to the best config. This isolates the effect of aggregation architecture. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it directly tests the most impactful architectural upgrade available within the current best configuration, and a positive result would open a productive exploitation path for the remaining 7 experiments, while a negative result would confirm avgpool suffices and redirect effort toward other variables (RNA encoder, fusion method, image encoder).

Evidence: config_012 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the best at 0.725 acc, showing transformer aggregation and multimodal fusion are strong. However, we've only tested one RNA encoder (scvi_n200) out of three available options. Uncertainty: whether scgpt, a learned single-cell genomics encoder, could outperform scvi_n200 in the multimodal pipeline. This experiment (config_024: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) holds all other hyperparameters at their best-known values and isolates the RNA encoder as the single variable. Resolving which RNA encoder is superior is critical because it will guide all remaining experiments (6 left) and directly impacts the ceiling of the best configuration. It is the highest-information experiment: a clear win or loss narrows the search space substantially.

Evidence: config_012 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the best at 0.725 acc, and scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + multiprofile is clearly the strongest combination (scgpt drops to 0.520, avgpool drops to 0.706, image-only is 0.332). Uncertainty: We have only tested 'weighted' fusion; 'concat' fusion is unexplored with this otherwise-optimal setup. This experiment (config_029) tests whether concat fusion outperforms weighted fusion while holding all other parameters at their known-best values. It is the best use of the next slot because it is the most direct exploitation of the current best configuration, isolates a single high-impact design variable (fusion strategy), and with 5 remaining experiments, confirming or ruling out concat fusion early will inform whether to further explore concat-based variants or continue refining the weighted path.

The current best is config_012 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. Evidence shows scvi_n200 is strongly preferred over scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520), transformer aggregation edges out avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706), and weighted fusion slightly beats concat (0.725 vs 0.721). The only major untested variable within this best-performing family is the image encoder. Config_019 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is a single-variable change from the best config, testing whether resnet50's different feature space could complement the RNA signal more effectively than imagenet_vit_l. This is the highest-value next experiment: it directly exploits the strongest configuration while probing the one remaining untested dimension, and the result will either yield a new best or confirm imagenet_vit_l as optimal, guiding the remaining 4 experiments toward the most promising sub-space.

Evidence: The current best (config_012: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, acc=0.725) clearly shows that scvi_n200 outperforms scgpt (0.520) and that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion is the strongest combination. However, pca_n2000 as an RNA encoder remains completely untested across all 6 experiments. Question: config_047 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) directly isolates the RNA encoder variable against the known-best baseline, testing whether a dimensionality-reduction-based representation can match or exceed the learned scvi_n200 encoder. Why best use of budget: With 3 experiments remaining after this one, resolving the RNA encoder question is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact design choice. If pca_n2000 performs comparably, it opens a broader search space; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 as the clear choice and lets us focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other variables (e.g., singleprofile, fusion). This single-variable test against the current best is the most information-efficient next step.

Evidence: The top-3 configs (012: 0.725, 029: 0.721, 019: 0.713) all use scvi_n200 + transformer, confirming these as the best RNA encoder and aggregation. However, config_019 (resnet50, weighted) shows the highest F1 (0.695) despite lower accuracy, suggesting resnet50 captures complementary information. The 2x2 grid of image_encoder × fusion under scvi_n200+transformer is: vit_l+weighted=0.725, vit_l+concat=0.721, resnet50+weighted=0.713, resnet50+concat=UNTESTED. Question: Does the resnet50+concat combination (config_028) exploit the F1 advantage seen with resnet50 while matching the near-equivalence of concat vs weighted fusion, potentially exceeding the current best of 0.725? Why: This is the single missing cell in the most promising design space, directly extending the strongest evidence (config_019's F1 signal). With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, completing this grid gives a definitive answer on whether a new best exists in this high-performing region, making it the highest-information-use experiment before final exploitation.

Evidence: The current best (config_012, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion in multiprofile mode. All top performers share these two encoders, and transformer aggregation clearly outperforms avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706). However, no singleprofile configuration has been tested with this best encoder pair. Question: config_009 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) tests whether removing the multiprofile aggregation step (aggregation=None) could be competitive or even superior, since singleprofile avoids potential information loss from averaging/transformer pooling across profiles. Why this is the best use: With only 1 experiment remaining after this, I need the highest-information experiment. Singleprofile is the only major architectural axis untested with the best encoders. If it matches or beats 0.725, it opens a new direction for the final experiment; if it underperforms, it firmly confirms multiprofile+transformer as optimal and lets the last experiment focus on fine-tuning (e.g., testing a minor fusion variant). This maximizes expected value under the tight budget.

Evidence: The top-3 performers (config_012: 0.7250, config_029: 0.7207, config_019: 0.7131) all use scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation, with imagenet_vit_l outperforming resnet50. Weighted fusion slightly edges concat. The best configuration (config_012) is already identified. Question: config_042 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the only untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion matrix for the best RNA+image encoder pair. While avgpool is expected to underperform transformer (~2% gap seen in config_001 vs config_012), testing this completes the design space for the top component combination and confirms whether the transformer advantage is consistent across fusion strategies. Rationale: As the final experiment (10/10), this provides the most informative closure on the primary design question (aggregation × fusion interaction for the best encoders) without wasting a slot on a configuration with weak prior evidence (scgpt or pca_n2000 RNA encoders, singleprofile, or unimodal settings all showed substantially lower performance).
